messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: 44-year-old male
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:

The patient presented at our primary care clinic with a lump in the right nipple associated with sharp pain. The mammogram revealed a 1.2 cm mass in the right retro areolar breast. Core needle biopsy was positive for invasive ductal carcinoma ER+ and PR+ and negative for HER2-. The patient underwent simple mastectomy and right sentinel lymph node biopsy. He received dose-dense adjuvant chemotherapy which was stopped after 3 doses of Taxanes. The lymph node biopsy came back positive for metastatic carcinoma, and the patient received radiation therapy. The patient was started on Tamoxifen therapy for>5 years.

Summary:

The 44-year-old male was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma stage IIA. He underwent simple mastectomy, right sentinel lymph node biopsy, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy. He was started on Tamoxifen therapy for>5 years. He denied any active complaints 3 years post diagnosis. The physical examination was positive for old healed lateral scar on the right chest. Genetic testing revealed no evidence of BRCA mutations or other evidence of familial breast cancer. The patient's annual mammographic screening and clinical exam of the contralateral breast were normal. He reported concerns of trouble maintaining erections and weight gain which were likely secondary to the effect of Tamoxifen.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for the episode is invasive ductal carcinoma of the right male breast, treated with mastectomy, sentinel node biopsy, chemotherapy, radiation and tamoxifen. It belongs to chapter C (neoplasms), and malignant neoplasm of breast is category C50, which covers male breast cancer (C50.9 and similar). The nodal metastasis is a secondary site, but the primary breast tumour is the condition chiefly treated, so it takes the principal diagnosis. The tamoxifen side effects are minor and do not outweigh the cancer.

CODE: C50
